Subject: Tenant segregation & VPC evidence request

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As part of our final SIG review we need concrete evidence for how Redwood enforces tenant segregation across regions and when customers use the Private (VPC) deployment option. Specifically the reviewers have asked for: 

- A diagram showing network boundaries (EU vs US) and how tenant traffic is routed when a customer pins an EU-only deployment.
- Confirmation of whether a single KMS key is used across regions or region-scoped keys (export of key metadata is fine).
- A CSV mapping of tenant IDs to hosting region for our sample account (redacted IDs acceptable) to validate isolation.
- Any SOC 2 system-description excerpt relevant to data flow and logical separation.

Can you provide these artifacts (PDF/CSV) or point me to a secure share? We are on a tight timeline — goal is to close next Wednesday (2026-06-24). If some items require an NDA or redaction, please advise.

Appreciate it —
Jane Roberts
Security Architect, Themis Health
security@themishealth.com

Hi team,

Attaching the artifacts requested — I pulled the exports and annotated the architecture diagram with the specific subnet/VPC boundary we use for Private deployments. Notes: 

- vpc-architecture-eu-us-annotated.pdf: shows two control-plane regions (us-west and eu-west), with private connector endpoints for EU tenants. The diagram also highlights our routing policy for pinned-region customers (traffic stays in-region; control-plane metadata is replicated but tenant data paths use region-local endpoints).
- kms-region-keys-export.csv: list of customer-managed and Redwood-managed key metadata (key id, region, type). We use region-scoped keys for customer data by default for Private deployments; hosted customers may have RBAC and envelope-wrapping with regional keys.
- tenant-mapping-evidence.csv: sample redacted tenant IDs mapped to hosting_region values (eu-west-1, us-west-2). Redaction applied per privacy policy; we replaced internal IDs with TID-XXX masked tokens.
- soc2-sysdescription-excerpt.pdf: excerpt focusing on logical separation and network controls.

Caveats: we do not export private key material. The csv contains only metadata and masked tenant IDs. If Themis requests raw, unmasked tenant IDs we need a signed data request and justification.

Action items: Mina to review for redaction/wording; Laura to confirm we can share SOC excerpt and approve the Drive link ACL. Sergio to publish a short-lived (7 day) link with restricted view.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachments: vpc-architecture-eu-us-annotated.pdf, kms-region-keys-export.csv, tenant-mapping-evidence.csv, soc2-sysdescription-excerpt.pdf]

Thanks for the clear checklist. We prepared a bundle that addresses each bullet in your note and placed the files on a restricted Drive folder (see links below). Summary of what we shared:

2) KMS: kms-region-keys-export.csv (metadata only; indicates region-scoped keys for Private deployments).
3) Tenant mapping: tenant-mapping-evidence.csv (redacted tenant tokens mapped to hosting_region values).
4) SOC 2 excerpt: soc2-sysdescription-excerpt.pdf (system description pages relevant to logical separation).

We will not provide any private key material or raw consumer identifiers without a signed data request. If you need further evidence (e.g., audit logs showing in-region egress), we can run a scoped export under a Data Processing Agreement addendum.
